subject: english
question:
阅读下面短文。

A Special Gift

My best friend Tom gave me a special gift on my birthday last year. It was not an expensive watch or a beautiful toy. It was a small notebook with a blue cover.

"Why did you give me a notebook?" I asked him, a little disappointed.

Tom smiled. "Open it and you will see."

I opened the notebook and found that Tom had written something on each page. On the first page, he wrote: "You are the bravest person I know." On the second page: "Remember when you helped the old lady carry her bags? That was really kind of you." On the third page: "You always make me laugh when I feel sad."

There were fifty pages in total, and each page had a different message about why I was special to him. Some messages made me laugh, and some made me cry.

"I wanted to give you something that would last longer than a toy," Tom said. "Whenever you feel sad or not good enough, just open this notebook and read it."

That notebook is still on my desk. Sometimes, when I have a bad day, I open it and read a few pages. It always makes me feel better.

(1) What did Tom give the writer as a birthday gift?
A. An expensive watch B. A blue notebook C. A beautiful toy D. A storybook

(2) How did the writer feel at first when he got the gift?
A. Excited B. Angry C. A little disappointed D. Very happy

(3) Tom says, "Whenever you feel sad or not good enough, just open this notebook." This suggests that Tom probably ___.
A. knew the writer sometimes felt insecure B. wanted the writer to study harder
C. didn't know what else to give D. had many extra notebooks

(4) Why did Tom choose this gift?
A. Because it was the most expensive B. Because he wanted to give something lasting
C. Because the writer asked for it D. Because he had no money

(5) Which of the following best describes the main idea of this story?
A. Expensive gifts are the best B. True friendship is more valuable than things
C. We should always give notebooks as gifts D. The writer is braver than Tom
analysis:
(1) B【考点】细节理解【解题思路】第一段明确写到"It was a small notebook with a blue cover."；A是作者期待但没有得到的；C是第一段列举但否定的选项
(2) C【考点】细节理解【解题思路】第二段写道"a little disappointed"，因为期待的是昂贵的手表或玩具；A和D与原文相反；B文中未提及
(3) A【考点】推理判断【解题思路】Tom说"每当觉得不够好时打开笔记本"——说明他知道作者有时会缺乏自信（felt insecure）；B"好好学习"与文中鼓励无关；C是消极猜测不符合Tom的用心；D有多余笔记本不是重点
(4) B【考点】推理判断【解题思路】Tom说"I wanted to give you something that would last longer than a toy"，说明他选择这个礼物是因为它能持久；A与Tom的想法相反；C和D文中未提及
(5) B【考点】主旨大意【解题思路】文章通过一个简单但有意义的礼物，传达了真正友谊的价值；A是文章反对的观点；C过于绝对化；D属于细节不能代表主旨
core_trap: 容易把局部细节误当成文章主旨，比如只看到"notebook"就选A，没有理解文章想表达的情感
mnemonic: 👉 答案就在原文里，定位关键句，比对选项找"同义替换"

subject: english
question:
阅读下面短文。

A Brave Decision

Last summer, 14-year-old Li Ming went to visit his grandmother in a small village in the mountains. The village was beautiful, with green hills, clear rivers, and fresh air. However, Li Ming noticed something that made him sad.

Many children in the village had to walk for more than an hour along a dangerous mountain road to get to school every day. During the rainy season, the road became muddy and slippery, and several children had fallen and gotten hurt. Some parents even kept their children at home because they were too worried.

Li Ming wanted to help. When he returned home, he told his classmates about the situation. Together, they decided to raise money to build a safer path for the village children. They organized a charity sale at school, selling handmade crafts, second-hand books, and baked goods. Li Ming also posted the story on social media, hoping more people would help.

To his surprise, the story quickly spread online. People from all over the country donated money and materials. A local construction company even offered to build the road for free. Within three months, a new concrete (混凝土) road was completed. The village children no longer had to worry about the dangerous walk to school.

When Li Ming visited his grandmother again during the winter holiday, the children of the village gave him a big thank-you card. It was covered with colorful handprints and heartfelt messages. Li Ming felt that this was the best gift he had ever received.

"The road is not just made of concrete," Li Ming said. "It is made of love and kindness from everyone who helped."

(1) Why did Li Ming feel sad when he visited the village?
A. Because his grandmother was sick B. Because the village was too small
C. Because children had to walk a dangerous road to school D. Because there was no food in the village

(2) What did Li Ming and his classmates do to help?
A. They organized a charity sale
C. ___PLACEHOLDER___ They went to build the road themselves D. They asked their parents for money

(3) How long did it take to build the new road?
A. One month B. Two months C. Three months D. One year

(4) What did the village children give Li Ming?
A. A new book B. A big thank-you card
C. Some money D. A handmade craft

(5) What is the author's main purpose in writing this passage?
A. One person cannot make a difference B. Young people can also help solve problems
C. Only adults can do great things D. It is better to wait for others to act
analysis:
(1) C【考点】细节理解【解题思路】第二段说"Many children in the village had to walk for more than an hour along a dangerous mountain road to get to school"；A奶奶生病文中未提及；B村庄小不是让他难过的事；D没有食物文中没说
(2) A【考点】细节理解【解题思路】第三段"They organized a charity sale at school"明确写了；A给政府写信是另一种解决方式但文中没有；C自己去修路不现实，文中是建筑公司建的；D找父母要钱文中没提
(3) C【考点】细节理解【解题思路】第四段"Within three months, a new concrete road was completed"；A和B时间太短；D一年太长
(4) B【考点】细节理解【解题思路】第五段"the children of the village gave him a big thank-you card"；A新书不是礼物；C钱文中没说孩子们给了钱；D手工艺品是义卖品不是回赠
(5) B【考点】推理判断【解题思路】整篇文章讲的是14岁少年发起行动，带动同学和社会力量解决问题，说明"年轻人也能帮忙解决社会问题"；A与文章主旨相反；C"只有大人能做大事"与文意矛盾；D等待他人行动是消极态度，不符合文章精神
core_trap: 第1题A"奶奶生病"是利用同情心的干扰项，原文并无此信息；第5题A"一个人改变不了什么"与文章展示的力量相反
mnemonic: 👉 故事类文章找"转折点"，行为背后的动机是考点

subject: english
question:
阅读下面短文。

My First Cooking Experience

Last Saturday, my parents went out to visit friends. I stayed at home alone. At around noon, I felt very hungry. I thought to myself, "Why not cook something by myself?"

I went to the kitchen and opened the fridge. There were eggs, tomatoes, and some rice. I decided to make tomato and egg fried rice. I had watched my mother do it many times, so I thought it would be easy.

First, I washed the tomatoes and cut them into small pieces. Then I broke two eggs into a bowl and mixed them. Next, I put some oil in the pan and turned on the stove. The oil got hot very quickly. I put the eggs in, but they started to make a loud noise and splash oil everywhere! I was so scared that I stepped back.

After the eggs were cooked, I added the tomatoes and the rice. I stirred them together, but the rice was not soft enough. The tomatoes were also a bit hard because I had not cooked them long enough.

When my parents came home, I showed them my "masterpiece." My mother tasted it and smiled. "It's not bad for your first time," she said. "But next time, cook the tomatoes a bit longer and use day-old rice. It tastes better."

My father also tried it and said, "Well, it's... interesting." I knew that meant it wasn't very good.

Even though my first cooking experience was not perfect, I felt proud. I learned that cooking is harder than it looks, and practice makes perfect!

(1) Why did the writer decide to cook?
A. His parents asked him to B. He felt hungry and was alone
C. He wanted to surprise his parents D. He likes cooking very much

(2) When the writer says "It's... interesting," his father probably means the food was ___.
A. delicious and creative B. not very tasty but he didn't want to hurt the writer's feelings
C. the best fried rice he ever had D. too salty to eat

(3) What problem did the writer have when cooking?
A. The oil splashed everywhere B. He cut his finger
C. He forgot to turn on the stove D. The eggs were broken

(4) What did the mother suggest for next time?
A. Use more oil B. Cook tomatoes longer and use day-old rice
C. Add more eggs D. Cook at a lower temperature

(5) What did the writer learn from this experience?
A. Cooking is easy B. He should never cook again
C. Cooking is harder than it looks D. Fried rice is the easiest dish
analysis:
(1) B【考点】细节理解【解题思路】第一段明确说"I felt very hungry"和"I stayed at home alone"；A是家长让孩子做的情景，与原文不符；C是结果而非原因；D文中没有提到他喜欢做饭
(2) B【考点】推理判断【解题思路】父亲说"interesting"加省略号和停顿（"Well, it's... interesting"），是一种委婉的否定——不好吃但不想打击孩子的积极性；A与后面"wasn't very good"矛盾；C与母亲说的"not bad"不同，父亲的评价更微妙；D过于直接，不会用"interesting"来形容
(3) A【考点】细节理解【解题思路】第三段描写"splash oil everywhere!"；A文中未提及受伤；C与原文矛盾（他确实开了火）；D是对"broke two eggs into a bowl"的误解，这是正常的打蛋操作
(4) B【考点】细节理解【解题思路】母亲说"cook the tomatoes a bit longer and use day-old rice"；A、C、D文中均未提及
(5) C【考点】主旨大意【解题思路】最后一段直接点明"cooking is harder than it looks, and practice makes perfect"；A与主旨相反；C是消极结论，文章态度是积极的；D过于绝对
core_trap: 第3题的D选项"The eggs were broken"是干扰项，"broke two eggs into a bowl"是正常的打蛋动作，不是问题
mnemonic: 👉 人物对话藏考点，注意委婉语和言外之意

subject: english
question:
阅读下面短文。

The Internet: A Double-Edged Sword

The Internet has changed our lives in many ways. It brings us both advantages and disadvantages.

On the one hand, the Internet makes our lives easier and more convenient. We can search for information, do online shopping, and communicate with friends far away. Students can use the Internet to help with their studies. For example, they can watch educational videos and take online courses. During the COVID-19 pandemic, many students studied at home thanks to online learning.

On the other hand, the Internet can cause problems. Some students spend too much time playing online games and watching short videos. This affects their studies and health. Some people also post bad information online, which can mislead others. Moreover, cyber bullying (网络欺凌) has become a serious problem among teenagers.

So, what should we do? First, we should limit our screen time. Experts suggest that teenagers should not spend more than two hours a day on entertainment screens. Second, we should learn to tell the difference between true and false information online. Third, if we experience cyber bullying, we should tell our parents or teachers immediately.

In conclusion, the Internet is a useful tool, but we must use it wisely. We are the masters of the Internet, not its slaves.

(1) Which of the following is an advantage of the Internet?
A. Spending time playing games B. Searching for information
C. Posting information online D. Making friends feel lonely

(2) What problem is mentioned about online entertainment?
A. It costs too much money B. It makes people feel lonely
C. It affects studies and health D. It causes eye problems only

(3) How long do experts suggest teenagers should spend on entertainment screens?
A. No more than two hours
C. ___PLACEHOLDER___ No more than three hours D. No more than four hours

(4) What should you do if you experience cyber bullying?
A. Fight back online B. Keep it a secret
C. Tell your parents or teachers D. Close your account

(5) What is the main idea of the last paragraph?
A. The Internet is bad for us B. We should stop using the Internet
C. We should use the Internet wisely D. The Internet is only for adults
analysis:
(1) B【考点】细节理解【解题思路】第二段列举了互联网的优点，包括"search for information"；A选项spending time playing games看似中性但文中明确说是负面影响；C选项posting information没有说明是advantage；D选项making friends feel lonely是网络欺凌的后果
(2) C【考点】细节理解【解题思路】第三段明确说"This affects their studies and health"；A文中未提及费用；B文中未提及孤独；D说"only"太绝对
(3) A【考点】细节理解【解题思路】第四段写"not spend more than two hours a day"，即不超过两小时；A太短，C和D太长
(4) C【考点】细节理解【解题思路】第四段建议"tell our parents or teachers immediately"；A会激化矛盾；B是消极做法；D文中未提及
(5) C【考点】段落主旨【解题思路】最后一段核心句是"we must use it wisely"；A和B与原文矛盾；D文中未提及
core_trap: 第1题容易混淆优势和缺点，注意审题问的是"advantage"
mnemonic: 👉 正反对比是利弊分析文的骨架，"however"两边答案相反

subject: english
question:
阅读下面短文。

A Letter to My Future Self

Dear Future Me,

I am writing this letter to you on April 10, 2026. I am 14 years old and I am in Grade 8. Right now, I am sitting in my room, thinking about what my life will be like in ten years.

First of all, I hope you are still studying hard. I know that you want to be a doctor, so I hope you have entered a good medical school. I also hope you are still playing the piano. Remember how much you love music? Don't give it up, no matter how busy you get.

I wonder if you still have the same friends. Tom, Lily, and Jack—do you still keep in touch with them? We have had so many good times together. I hope you haven't forgotten our promise to travel the world together someday.

Right now, I am worried about my English grades. I hope by the time you read this, your English has improved a lot. Maybe you can even speak English fluently and have traveled to some English-speaking countries.

I also hope you are healthy and happy. Please remember to exercise regularly and eat well. Don't work too hard. Take time to enjoy life.

No matter what happens, I believe in you. You were brave enough to write this letter, and you will be brave enough to face any challenges in the future.

Love,
Your 14-Year-Old Self

(1) Who wrote this letter?
A. A 14-year-old student C. ___PLACEHOLDER___ A piano teacher D. A 24-year-old person

(2) What does the writer want to be in the future?
A. A teacher B. A musician C. A doctor D. A writer

(3) In the letter, "No matter what happens, I believe in you" shows that the writer is ___.
A. worried about the future B. confident and encouraging towards himself
C. giving up on his dreams D. asking for help from others

(4) When does the writer hope the reader will read this letter?
A. In five years B. In eight years C. In ten years D. In fourteen years

(5) What is the tone of this letter?
A. Sad and hopeless B. Angry and frustrated
C. Hopeful and encouraging D. Bored and uninterested
analysis:
(1) A【考点】细节理解【解题思路】第二段自述"I am 14 years old and I am in Grade 8"；A是梦想不是现实；C和D都不是写信时的身份
(2) C【考点】细节理解【解题思路】第三段写道"I know that you want to be a doctor"；A、B、D文中未提及
(3) B【考点】推理判断【解题思路】"I believe in you"是对未来自己的鼓励，表达了对自我的信心；A与"believe in"的积极态度矛盾；C与"brave enough"矛盾；D是向别人求助，但这是写给自己的信
(4) C【考点】推理判断【解题思路】第二段说"thinking about what my life will be like in ten years"，说明是写给十年后的自己；写信人14岁，十年后24岁
(5) C【考点】推理判断【解题思路】全文用"I hope"、"I believe in you"、"brave enough"等表达，语气充满希望和鼓励；A、B、D与文章情感基调完全不符
core_trap: 第1题的A选项"A future doctor"是混淆项，因为文章提到了想当医生，但写信时的身份是学生
mnemonic: 👉 书信体关注"I hope/I wonder/I believe"，情感态度是关键

question:
阅读下面短文。

Save the Elephants

Elephants are the largest animals on land. They are also one of the most intelligent animals in the world. However, these amazing animals are in danger.

There are two main reasons why elephants are in danger. First, people cut down too many trees in forests. Elephants lose their homes and have nowhere to go. Second, some people hunt elephants for their ivory (象牙). They kill elephants and take their tusks (长牙) to sell for money. Every year, thousands of elephants are killed this way.

If we do not take action, elephants may disappear from the earth forever. Here are some things we can do to help:

• Never buy anything made of ivory. If no one buys ivory, hunters will have no reason to kill elephants.
• Support organizations that protect elephants. We can donate money or volunteer to help.
• Tell others about the importance of protecting elephants. The more people know, the more help elephants will get.

China has already taken steps to protect elephants. In 2017, China banned (禁止) all ivory trade. This was a great step forward. Many other countries are also working hard to protect these wonderful animals.

Remember: elephants are our friends, not our property. Let's work together to save them!

(1) Why are elephants in danger?
A. Because of climate change B. Because they eat too much
C. Because of losing homes and hunting D. Because they are not intelligent

(2) What do hunters kill elephants for?
A. Their meat and skin B. Their tusks to make jewelry
C. Their ivory D. Their fur for clothing

(3) What is one important thing we should do to protect elephants?
A. Buy more ivory products B. Never buy anything made of ivory
C. Hunt elephants ourselves D. Cut down more trees

(4) What can we infer (推断) from the sentence "If no one buys ivory, hunters will have no reason to kill elephants"?
A. Ivory is very cheap B. The demand for ivory is the main reason elephants are killed
C. Hunters kill elephants for fun D. Elephants are not afraid of hunters

(5) What is the purpose of this passage?
A. To introduce elephants B. To compare elephants with other animals To tell a story about elephants D. To ask people to protect elephants
C.
analysis:
(1) C【考点】细节理解【解题思路】第三段列出了两个原因：失去家园和被猎杀；A是文中未提及的原因；B和D与原文矛盾
(2) C【考点】细节理解【解题思路】第三段说"hunt elephants for their ivory"；A是某些地区猎杀其他动物的原因但文中未提到猎象是为了肉和皮；B选项to make jewelry是用象牙做首饰虽然合理但原文用的是ivory不是jewelry，属于合理推测但非直接对应；D fur指毛皮，大象没有毛皮
(4) B【考点】推理判断【解题思路】这句话的逻辑是：没有买家→猎人没有理由→不会猎杀，说明市场需求是猎杀的根本动力；A与ivory的珍贵性矛盾；C"for fun"文中未提，猎杀是为了赚钱；D与文章主题无关
(3) B【考点】细节理解【解题思路】第四段第一条建议就是"Never buy anything made of ivory"；A是反面做法；C和D是破坏行为
(5) D【考点】写作目的【解题思路】全文介绍了大象面临的威胁并提出保护建议，目的是呼吁保护大象；A只是背景信息；C和D不是主要目的
core_trap: 第1题需要找到两个原因，C选项"losing homes and hunting"涵盖了两个要点
mnemonic: 👉 环保主题抓"因果关系"，原因和解决办法是常考点

subject: english
question:
阅读下面短文。

The School Sports Meet

Our school held its annual sports meet last Friday. The weather was perfect—sunny but not too hot. All the students were excited because this was one of the biggest events of the year.

The sports meet started at 8:00 in the morning. First, our principal gave a short speech. Then, the opening ceremony began. Each class marched around the track, shouting slogans and waving flags.

There were many events, including the 100-meter race, the 800-meter race, long jump, high jump, and relay race. I took part in the 800-meter race. When the starting gun fired, I ran as fast as I could. However, by the second lap, I was very tired. I wanted to give up, but hearing my classmates cheering for me gave me strength. I pushed myself to finish the race and came in fifth place.

The most exciting moment was the 4×100-meter relay race. Our class team practiced for weeks before the meet. When the last runner, Li Hua, received the baton, he was behind the leader. But he ran with all his might and crossed the finish line first! Our whole class jumped up and cheered. We won first place in the relay!

At the end of the day, our class came second overall. Although we didn't win first place, everyone was happy because we had tried our best and worked together as a team.

The sports meet taught me an important lesson: winning is not the most important thing. What matters more is doing your best and never giving up.

(1) What does "I pushed myself to finish the race" tell us about the writer?
A. He was naturally good at running B. He gave up during the race
C. He forced himself to continue despite being tired D. He won the race easily

(2) Which race did the writer take part in?
A. The 100-meter race B. The 800-meter race C. The relay race D. The long jump

(3) What place did the writer get in his race?
A. First place B. Second place C. Third place D. Fifth place

(4) Who won the relay race for their class?
A. The writer B. Li Hua C. The principal D. Tom

(5) What lesson did the writer learn?
A. Winning is everything B. Teamwork helps achieve better results
C. Doing your best and never giving up D. Sports are more important than studies
analysis:
(1) C【考点】推理判断【解题思路】"pushed myself"意为"强迫自己/咬牙坚持"，结合前文"I was very tired. I wanted to give up"，说明虽然很累想放弃但还是坚持了；A与"very tired"矛盾；B与"pushed myself to finish"矛盾；D与"came in fifth place"矛盾
(2) B【考点】细节理解【解题思路】第三段说"I took part in the 800-meter race"；A虽然文中提到了，但不是作者参加的项目；C是Li Hua参加的
(3) D【考点】细节理解【解题思路】第三段最后说"came in fifth place"；注意不要混淆作者的名次和班级的总体名次（第二名）
(4) B【考点】细节理解【解题思路】第四段描述"the last runner, Li Hua...crossed the finish line first"；A是作者参加800米的；C和D与此无关
(5) C【考点】主旨大意【解题思路】最后一段点明"What matters more is doing your best and never giving up"；A是文章反对的观点；B虽然合理但不是核心教训，文章强调的是个人努力和坚持而非团队成绩；D文章未涉及
core_trap: 第3题容易把"班级第二名"和"个人第五名"混淆，注意区分不同层面的名次
mnemonic: 👉 动作描写细节多，"push/force/hardly"等动词含深意

question:
阅读下面短文。

The Power of Habits

A habit is something we do regularly without thinking too much about it. Some habits are good, like brushing our teeth every morning, and some are bad, like biting our nails.

Scientists say that it takes about 21 days to form a new habit. This means that if you want to develop a good habit, you need to keep doing it for at least three weeks. For example, if you want to start reading for 30 minutes before bed, do it every day for 21 days. After that, it will feel natural.

However, breaking a bad habit can be much harder. One helpful method is to replace a bad habit with a good one. For instance, if you always eat snacks while watching TV, try eating fruit instead of chips. Another method is to change your environment. If you want to stop playing phone games before sleep, put your phone in another room.

Good habits can change our lives. Students who have the habit of reviewing lessons every day usually get better grades. People who exercise regularly tend to be healthier and happier. The key is to start small and be patient.

Remember, you are what you repeatedly do. So choose your habits carefully!

(1) According to scientists, how long does it take to form a new habit?
A. About 7 days B. About 14 days C. About 21 days D. About 30 days

(2) What is one method to break a bad habit?
A. Ignore it B. Replace it with a good one
C. Tell your friends D. Wait for it to go away

(3) If you want to stop using your phone before sleep, what should you do?
A. Turn it off B. Delete the games C. Put it in another room D. Give it to a friend

(4) Which of the following is an example of a good habit?
A. Biting nails B. Eating snacks while watching TV
C. Playing phone games before sleep D. Reviewing lessons every day

(5) What does "you are what you repeatedly do" mean?
A. You can do anything B. Your habits define who you are
C. You should do things repeatedly D. You should try different things
analysis:
(1) C【考点】细节理解【解题思路】第二段开头说"it takes about 21 days to form a new habit"；A和B太短，D是文章后面提到的阅读时间
(2) B【考点】细节理解【解题思路】第三段提出"replace a bad habit with a good one"；A、C、D都不是文中提到的方法
(3) C【考点】细节理解【解题思路】第三段举了这个例子"put your phone in another room"；A、B、D虽然也可能有效，但不是文中提到的建议
(4) D【考点】推理判断【解题思路】第四段提到"reviewing lessons every day usually get better grades"，这是好习惯；A、B、C都是文中举的反面例子
(5) B【考点】句意理解【解题思路】"You are what you repeatedly do"意思是"你反复做的事定义了你是谁"，即习惯决定品格；A和C是字面误解；D偏离了原意
core_trap: 第5题是谚语理解题，不能按字面意思翻译，需要理解深层含义

question:
阅读下面短文。

A Visit to the Science Museum

Last weekend, our class went on a trip to the City Science Museum. It was my first time visiting a science museum, and I was very excited.

When we arrived, a guide showed us around. The museum has four floors. On the first floor, there is a space exhibition. We saw models of planets, rockets, and even a real spacesuit! I learned that astronauts wear spacesuits that weigh about 120 kilograms on Earth, but on the Moon, they feel much lighter because of the lower gravity.

On the second floor, there is a robotics exhibition. We watched a robot play chess with a visitor. The robot won the game! There was also a robot that could dance and speak in three languages. I was amazed by how smart these robots were.

The third floor had an environmental science exhibition. It showed how pollution affects our planet and what we can do to protect the environment. One display showed that if everyone in China saved one piece of paper every day, we could save millions of trees each year.

On the fourth floor, there was a hands-on experiment area. We could do simple science experiments ourselves. I made a small volcano that actually erupted (爆发)! It was the most fun part of the trip.

Before we left, we watched a 3D movie about the ocean in the museum's theater. It felt like we were really swimming with the fish!

This trip made me realize that science is not just something in textbooks. It is everywhere in our daily lives, and it is really interesting!

(1) What does "hands-on" mean in "hands-on experiment area"?
A. Done by yourself B. Dangerous C. Done with machines D. Only for scientists

(2) What did the writer see on the first floor?
A. Robots playing chess B. Environmental exhibitions
C. Models of planets and rockets D. A 3D movie about the ocean

(3) How much does a spacesuit weigh on Earth?
A. About 95 kilograms B. About 110 kilograms
C. About 120 kilograms D. About 150 kilograms

(4) Which floor did the writer enjoy the most?
A. The first floor B. The second floor
C. The third floor D. The fourth floor

(5) What did the writer learn from this trip?
A. Science is boring B. Science is only in textbooks
C. Science is interesting and everywhere in daily life D. Museums are not worth visiting

(4) D【考点】推理判断【解题思路】第五段说"It was the most fun part of the trip"，描述的是四楼的实验区；注意"most fun"=enjoyed the most
(5) C【考点】主旨大意【解题思路】最后一段说"science is not just something in textbooks. It is everywhere in our daily lives, and it is really interesting"；A、B、D与原文意思相反

question:
阅读下面短文。

My Neighbor, Mr. Wang

Mr. Wang is my neighbor. He is about 70 years old, but he looks much younger. Every morning, he gets up at 5:30 and goes to the park near our apartment. He runs for 30 minutes and then practices Tai Chi for another 30 minutes. He says this routine keeps him healthy and energetic.

Mr. Wang is retired. Before he retired, he was a Chinese teacher at a middle school. Even though he no longer teaches, he still loves learning. He reads books every day and has recently started learning how to use a computer and the Internet. "It's never too old to learn," he often says with a smile.

Mr. Wang is also very kind and helpful. Last month, when my parents were both sick with the flu, Mr. Wang cooked meals for our family every day until they got better. He makes the best dumplings in the world! He also helps take care of the plants in our apartment building's garden.

One thing I admire most about Mr. Wang is his positive attitude towards life. Even when he faces difficulties, he always stays optimistic. He told me once, "Life is like a mirror. If you smile at it, it will smile back at you."

I feel very lucky to have Mr. Wang as my neighbor. He has taught me that age is just a number and that a positive attitude can make life wonderful.

(1) What does Mr. Wang do every morning?
A. He goes shopping B. He runs and practices Tai Chi
C. He reads books D. He cooks breakfast

(2) What was Mr. Wang's job before retirement?
A. A doctor B. A cook C. A Chinese teacher D. A gardener

(3) What new skill has Mr. Wang started learning?
A. Cooking B. Gardening C. A foreign language D. Using a computer and the Internet

A. We should look at ourselves often B. Our attitude towards life affects our happiness

question:
阅读下面短文。

The Moon Cake Story

The Mid-Autumn Festival is one of the most important traditional festivals in China. It falls on the 15th day of the eighth lunar month. On this day, the moon is believed to be the fullest and brightest of the year.

There is a famous legend about the Mid-Autumn Festival. Long ago, there were ten suns in the sky. It was so hot that people could not grow crops. A hero named Hou Yi shot down nine of the suns with his bow and arrow. As a reward, the Queen Mother of the West gave him an elixir (仙药) that could make him live forever.

Hou Yi had a beautiful wife named Chang'e. He loved her very much and did not want to leave her alone. So he asked Chang'e to keep the elixir for him.

One day, a bad man came to steal the elixir while Hou Yi was out. To protect it, Chang'e drank the elixir herself. She immediately became very light and flew up to the Moon. Hou Yi was heartbroken. He looked up at the Moon and could see Chang'e's shadow there.

Since then, Hou Yi would prepare Chang'e's favorite foods and fruits on the night of the full moon. This became the tradition of eating moon cakes and admiring the moon during the Mid-Autumn Festival.

Today, moon cakes come in many different flavors. The most traditional ones have sweet fillings like lotus seed paste (莲蓉) or red bean paste. Modern moon cakes can have ice cream, chocolate, or even fruit fillings.

(1) When is the Mid-Autumn Festival?
A. The 15th day of the eighth lunar month
C. ___PLACEHOLDER___ The eighth day of the eighth lunar month D. The first full moon of the year

(2) What did Hou Yi do to help people?
A. He gave them food B. He found water for them
C. He shot down nine suns D. He gave them the elixir

(3) Why did Chang'e fly to the Moon?
A. She wanted to live forever like Hou Yi B. She drank the elixir to protect it
C. The bad man forced her to drink it D. She wanted to see the Moon

(4) What can we learn about traditional moon cakes from the passage?
A. They only come in two flavors B. They are no longer popular today
C. They usually have sweet fillings D. They are made with chocolate

(5) What is this passage mainly about?
A. Traditional Chinese festivals B. The legend and traditions of Mid-Autumn Festival
C. How to make moon cakes D. Famous Chinese legends
analysis:
(1) A【考点】细节理解【解题思路】第一段明确说"the 15th day of the eighth lunar month"；A七月十五是中元节，容易混淆；C把月和日反过来；D"一年第一个满月"指元宵节，都是中国传统节日日期，迷惑性更强
(2) C【考点】细节理解【解题思路】第二段说"Hou Yi shot down nine of the suns with his bow and arrow"；A、B、D文中未提及
(3) B【考点】细节理解【解题思路】第四段"To protect it, Chang'e drank the elixir herself"是直接原因；A是仙药的效果不是她喝药的原因；C强盗逼她喝不对，是她自己喝的；D想看月亮与事实不符
(4) C【考点】推理判断【解题思路】第六段"The most traditional ones have sweet fillings like lotus seed paste or red bean paste"，传统月饼通常有甜馅料；A"only"过于绝对，原文用"like"表示举例而非穷举；B"不再流行"与原文矛盾；D巧克力是现代口味
(5) B【考点】主旨大意【解题思路】文章围绕中秋节的传说（嫦娥奔月）和传统（月饼）展开；A"中国传统节日"范围太宽；C只涉及月饼是片面内容；D"著名传说"包括了非中秋节的内容，范围偏大

question:
阅读下面短文。

An Unforgettable Experience

Last summer vacation, I went to a small village in the mountains with my parents. It was far from the city, and there was no Internet or TV. At first, I felt very bored.

However, things changed on the second day. An old man named Grandpa Li took me to catch fish in the river. He taught me how to use a simple fishing net. At first, I was not good at it. The fish kept slipping away. But Grandpa Li was very patient. He told me, "Fishing needs patience. If you wait quietly, the fish will come."

After about an hour, I finally caught my first fish! It was small, but I was so excited. I showed it to everyone proudly. That evening, Grandpa Li helped me cook the fish. It was the most delicious fish I had ever tasted.

During the next few days, I learned many things. I learned how to pick vegetables in the garden, how to climb trees safely, and how to tell the direction by looking at the stars at night. I also made friends with some children in the village. We played together in the fields and caught fireflies at night.

On the last night, I lay on the grass and looked at the stars. There were so many of them! In the city, I could never see so many stars because of the lights. The sky looked like a black blanket covered with diamonds.

When it was time to leave, I didn't want to go. I hugged Grandpa Li and promised to visit again next summer.

This trip taught me that the best things in life are often the simplest ones. You don't need the Internet or TV to be happy. Sometimes, all you need is nature and good company.

(1) How did the writer feel at first about the village?
A. Excited B. Happy C. Bored D. Scared

(2) What did Grandpa Li teach the writer?
A. How to cook B. How to catch fish
C. How to climb mountains D. How to use a computer

(3) Grandpa Li said "Fishing needs patience." What does this tell us about Grandpa Li?
A. He was a professional fisherman B. He was impatient with the writer
C. He understood that good things require waiting D. He wanted to go home early

(4) What could the writer see in the village but not in the city?
A. Many stars B. Many fish C. Many trees D. Many children

(5) What is the main lesson from this story?
A. City life is better than country life B. The simplest things can be the best
C. We should always go fishing D. The Internet is bad for us
analysis:
(1) C【考点】细节理解【解题思路】第一段说"At first, I felt very bored"；A和B与原文相反；D文中未提及
(2) B【考点】细节理解【解题思路】第二段说"Grandpa Li took me to catch fish in the river"和"taught me how to use a simple fishing net"；A和C是后面学的；D在村里没有
(3) C【考点】推理判断【解题思路】"Fishing needs patience. If you wait quietly, the fish will come"说明Grandpa Li认为耐心等待会有回报，这是他的人生智慧；A文中未说他是专业渔民；B与"very patient"矛盾；D与后面耐心教导矛盾
(4) A【考点】细节理解【解题思路】第五段对比了城乡，说"In the city, I could never see so many stars because of the lights"；B、C、D城里也有
(5) B【考点】主旨大意【解题思路】最后一段点明"the best things in life are often the simplest ones"；A文中没有比较城乡好坏；C和D太片面
core_trap: 第5题C和D都是文章涉及的内容，但不能代表主旨，主旨是"最简单的东西往往最美好"

Teenagers and Part-Time Jobs

In many countries, teenagers can have part-time jobs. In China, more and more teenagers are also starting to work part-time during holidays. But is it a good idea?

There are several advantages of part-time jobs. First, teenagers can earn their own money. This helps them understand the value of money and learn to manage it wisely. Second, working part-time can help teenagers develop important skills like communication, teamwork, and time management. Third, having a part-time job gives teenagers a chance to experience the real world before they graduate.

However, there are also disadvantages. Some people worry that working too much may affect teenagers' studies. If a student spends too much time working, they may not have enough time to do homework or review lessons. Besides, some jobs may not be safe for teenagers. For example, working in a factory or on a construction site can be dangerous.

In China, the law says that teenagers under 16 years old are not allowed to work. For those who are 16 or older, they can only do light work that does not affect their studies or health.

In my opinion, having a part-time job can be a good experience if done properly. Teenagers should choose jobs that are safe and suitable. They should also make sure that work does not affect their studies. After all, education is still the most important thing for teenagers.

(1) What is the main topic of this passage?
A. How to find a good job B. Whether teenagers should have part-time jobs
C. How to manage money D. How to study and work at the same time

C. Experiencing the real world D. Getting better grades

(4) C【考点】细节理解【解题思路】第四段说"teenagers under 16 years old are not allowed to work"，反过来就是16岁及以上可以；A和B太小

question:
阅读下面短文。

The Great Wall of China

The Great Wall of China is one of the greatest wonders of the world. It is also one of the most famous symbols of China. Every year, millions of tourists from all over the world come to visit it.

The Great Wall has a very long history. The first parts of the wall were built more than 2,000 years ago, during the Qin Dynasty. The emperor Qin Shi Huang ordered the building of the wall to protect China from enemies in the north. Most of the Great Wall that we can see today was built during the Ming Dynasty, about 600 years ago.

The Great Wall is very long. It stretches (延伸) for over 21,000 kilometers across northern China. It starts from the east coast and ends in the west, crossing mountains, deserts, and grasslands. Because of its great length, it is often called "The Long Wall" or "The Ten Thousand Li Wall" (万里长城).

Building the Great Wall was a huge project. Millions of workers, including soldiers, farmers, and prisoners, worked on it. Many of them worked in very difficult conditions. Sadly, a large number of workers died during the construction (建造).

Today, the Great Wall is a UNESCO World Heritage Site (世界文化遗产). It is not just a wall—it represents the wisdom, strength, and spirit of the Chinese people.

However, parts of the Great Wall are being damaged by tourists, natural erosion (侵蚀), and illegal construction. The Chinese government and many organizations are working hard to protect and restore (修复) it.

When you visit the Great Wall, please remember: don't carve (刻) your name on the bricks, don't litter, and respect this great piece of history.

(1) When were the first parts of the Great Wall built?
A. About 600 years ago B. About 1,000 years ago
C. More than 2,000 years ago D. About 500 years ago

(2) Why was the Great Wall built?
A. For tourists to visit B. To protect China from enemies
C. To show China's power D. To help farmers travel

(3) How long is the Great Wall?
A. About 6,000 kilometers B. About 10,000 kilometers
C. About 15,000 kilometers D. Over 21,000 kilometers

(4) What is the Great Wall a symbol of?
A. Chinese food B. Chinese festivals
C. The wisdom and spirit of Chinese people D. Chinese art

(5) What should you NOT do when visiting the Great Wall?
A. Take photos B. Carve your name on the bricks
C. Walk on it D. Learn its history
analysis:
(1) C【考点】细节理解【解题思路】第二段说"more than 2,000 years ago, during the Qin Dynasty"；A是明代修建的时间；B和D不准确
(2) B【考点】细节理解【解题思路】第二段说"to protect China from enemies in the north"；A是现代功能不是修建目的；C和D不是主要原因
(3) D【考点】细节理解【解题思路】第三段给出"over 21,000 kilometers"；A、B、C的数字都与原文不符
(4) C【考点】推理判断【解题思路】第五段说"it represents the wisdom, strength, and spirit of the Chinese people"；A、B、D不是长城的象征
(5) B【考点】细节理解【解题思路】最后一段说"don't carve your name on the bricks"；A、C、D都是正常行为

question:
阅读下面短文。

The Girl Who Was Afraid of Speaking

Lily was a quiet girl. She was good at writing, but she was afraid of speaking in public. Whenever the teacher asked her to answer a question in class, her face turned red and she could not say a word.

One day, the teacher announced a speech competition. "Everyone in our class must take part," the teacher said. Lily's heart sank. She went home and told her mother about it.

"I can't do it, Mom. I'm too scared," Lily said.

Her mother held her hand and said, "Being brave doesn't mean you are not scared. It means you do it even though you are scared."

Lily thought about her mother's words. She decided to face her fear. Every evening after dinner, she stood in front of the mirror and practiced her speech. At first, she made many mistakes and felt embarrassed. But she kept practicing. Day after day, she got better and better.

On the day of the competition, Lily was very nervous. When it was her turn, her legs were shaking. She took a deep breath and started to speak. At first, her voice was small, but as she continued, she became more and more confident.

When she finished, the whole class clapped (鼓掌). The teacher said, "Well done, Lily! That was an excellent speech!"

Lily didn't win first place, but she won something more important—she conquered (战胜) her fear. From that day on, she was no longer afraid of speaking in public.

(1) What was Lily's problem?
A. She was not good at writing B. She was afraid of the teacher She was not good at studying D. She was afraid of speaking in public
C.

(2) What did Lily's mother tell her about being brave?
A. Brave people are never scared B. Being brave means doing it even when scared
C. She should not join the competition D. She should practice writing instead

(3) "Her legs were shaking" when it was her turn. This detail shows that ___.
A. Lily was sick that day B. Lily was still afraid but chose to face her fear
C. Lily didn't practice enough D. The teacher made a wrong decision

(4) What happened during Lily's speech?

Here are some tips for using social media wisely:

question:

How Does the Internet Work?

Have you ever wondered how the Internet works? When you type a website address in your browser and press Enter, the webpage appears almost instantly. But what happens behind the scenes?

The Internet is a global network (全球网络) of computers connected together. When you send a message or request a webpage, your computer sends the request through your Wi-Fi or cable to your Internet Service Provider (ISP). The ISP then sends your request to a server—a powerful computer that stores the webpage you want.

Here is a simple way to understand it: imagine you want to send a letter to a friend. You write the letter (your request), put it in an envelope (data packets), give it to the post office (your ISP), and the post office delivers it to your friend's house (the server). Your friend then sends a reply back to you (the webpage).

All the data on the Internet is broken into small pieces called "packets" (数据包). Each packet travels through different routes to reach its destination. When all the packets arrive, they are put back together to form the complete message or webpage.

The speed of the Internet depends on several factors: your connection type (Wi-Fi, 4G, 5G, cable), the distance to the server, and how many people are using the network at the same time. That is why the Internet is sometimes slow during peak hours.

The Internet was invented in 1969 in the United States. At that time, it was called ARPANET and was used by the military and universities. It was not until the 1990s that the Internet became popular for everyday people.

(1) What does ISP stand for?
A. Internet Safety Program B. Internet Service Provider
C. International Sports Party D. Internet Shopping Platform

(2) In the letter analogy (比喻), what does the "post office" represent?
A. Your computer B. The server C. The ISP D. The webpage

A. Small pieces of data B. Large files
C. Computer programs D. Websites

(4) Why might the Internet be slow sometimes?
A. Because the computer is too old B. Because too many people are using it
C. Because the weather is bad D. Because the server is turned off

(5) When did the Internet become popular for ordinary people?
A. In 1969 B. In the 1970s C. In the 1980s D. In the 1990s

(1) B【考点】细节理解【解题思路】第二段解释了"Internet Service Provider (ISP)"；A、C、D是编造的全称
(2) C【考点】细节理解【解题思路】第三段明确说"give it to the post office (your ISP)"；A是写信人；B是收信人地址；D是回信内容
(3) A【考点】细节理解【解题思路】第四段说"data is broken into small pieces called 'packets'"；B与"small pieces"矛盾；C和D不是数据包的含义
(4) B【考点】细节理解【解题思路】第五段说"how many people are using the network at the same time"；A、C、D文中未提及
(5) D【考点】细节理解【解题思路】最后一段说"It was not until the 1990s that the Internet became popular"；A是ARPANET诞生的时间不是流行的时间

Traditional Chinese Medicine

Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) has a history of more than 2,000 years. It is an important part of Chinese culture and is becoming more and more popular around the world.

One of the most famous TCM treatments is acupuncture (针灸). Acupuncture uses very thin needles (针) that are put into specific points on the body. It can help relieve pain and treat many health problems. Today, acupuncture is practiced in over 180 countries.

Another important part of TCM is herbal medicine (草药). TCM doctors use hundreds of different herbs (草药) to make medicines. These medicines are usually boiled into soup and drunk. Some common herbs include ginseng (人参), goji berries (枸杞), and honeysuckle (金银花).

TCM also emphasizes (强调) prevention (预防). There is a famous saying: "A good doctor treats the illness before it happens." This means TCM believes it is better to prevent illness than to cure it. TCM suggests that people should eat according to the seasons, exercise regularly, and keep a balanced lifestyle.

In 2015, Tu Youyou, a Chinese scientist, won the Nobel Prize for discovering artemisinin (青蒿素), which is used to treat malaria (疟疾). This discovery was inspired by traditional Chinese herbal medicine.

However, TCM also faces challenges. Some people question whether TCM is scientific enough. Scientists are doing more research to prove the effectiveness (有效性) of TCM treatments.

Weather and Climate

Many people confuse weather and climate, but they are actually different things.

Weather refers to (指的是) the conditions of the atmosphere (大气) at a specific time and place. For example, it might be sunny today but rainy tomorrow. Weather can change very quickly. When you check the weather forecast (天气预报) on your phone, you are getting information about the weather.

Climate, on the other hand, refers to the average (平均的) weather conditions over a long period of time—usually 30 years or more. For example, Beijing has a continental climate, which means it has hot summers and cold winters. Climate does not change quickly.

The difference between weather and climate can be understood with a simple example. Weather is like your mood (心情)—it changes from day to day. Climate is like your personality (性格)—it stays mostly the same over a long time.

Climate change is one of the biggest problems facing the world today. Because of human activities like burning fossil fuels (化石燃料) and cutting down forests, the Earth's average temperature is rising. This is causing many problems:
• Ice in the North and South Poles is melting
• Sea levels are rising
• Extreme weather events (like floods and droughts) are becoming more common
• Many plants and animals are losing their habitats

What can we do to help? Here are some simple actions:
• Walk, ride a bike, or take public transport instead of driving
• Turn off lights and electronics when you are not using them
• Plant more trees
• Reduce, reuse, and recycle

My First Calligraphy Lesson

When I was twelve, my parents signed me up for a traditional Chinese calligraphy (书法) class. At first, I was not interested at all. "Why do I need to learn this?" I complained. "Nobody writes with a brush anymore!"

The first day of class, our teacher, Mr. Zhang, showed us some famous calligraphy works by ancient masters. The characters looked like art—each stroke (笔画) had its own rhythm and beauty. I was surprised that writing could be so elegant.

Then Mr. Zhang gave each of us a brush, some ink, and rice paper. "The most important thing in calligraphy," he said, "is patience (耐心) and concentration (专注). Your mind must be calm and steady, just like the brush."

I dipped the brush in the ink and tried to write the character "yong" (永), which contains all the basic strokes in Chinese. My first attempt was terrible. The lines were shaky, and the ink blotched (洇开) everywhere. I felt frustrated and wanted to give up.

"Don't rush," Mr. Zhang said gently. "Every master was once a beginner. Practice makes progress, not perfection." He then guided my hand slowly, showing me how to control the pressure and speed of the brush. With his help, my second attempt looked much better.

Over the next few months, I practiced calligraphy every Saturday. Gradually, my strokes became smoother and more confident. I even won third prize in a city-wide calligraphy competition! Now, calligraphy has become my favorite hobby. I find it relaxing and meaningful.

Looking back, I am glad my parents pushed me to try something new. Sometimes the things we resist at first turn out to be the most rewarding experiences of our lives.

C. Calligraphy is easy to learn D. Competition is the best way to improve

(1) B【考点】细节理解【解题思路】第一段说"At first, I was not interested at all"；A兴奋与原文相反；C有一点好奇是后来参观作品时的感受，不是一开始；D紧张文中未提及
(2) A【考点】细节理解【解题思路】第三段Mr. Zhang说"The most important thing in calligraphy is patience and concentration"；A速度和天赋不是老师强调的；B好看的纸是工具不是核心；D昂贵的笔更不是重点

Do you skip breakfast (不吃早餐) because you are in a hurry in the morning? If so, you are not alone. Many students skip breakfast to save time. However, this is a very bad habit.

If you really don't have time for a full breakfast, at least grab something quick, like a banana, a boiled egg, or a glass of milk. It is much better than eating nothing.

Remember: don't trade your health for a few extra minutes of sleep. A good breakfast is the best start to a good day.

Have you ever thought about volunteering? Volunteering means giving your time and energy to help others without getting paid. It may sound like you are only giving, but actually, you receive a lot in return.

First, volunteering helps you learn new skills. When you volunteer at a hospital, you learn how to communicate with patients. When you volunteer at an animal shelter, you learn how to take care of animals. These skills can be useful in your future career.

Second, volunteering helps you make new friends. You meet people from different backgrounds who share the same passion (热情) for helping others. Many volunteers become lifelong friends.

Third, volunteering makes you feel good about yourself. Studies show that helping others can reduce stress and increase happiness. When you see the positive impact (影响) you make on someone's life, you feel proud and fulfilled.

There are many ways to volunteer:
• Help the elderly: Visit nursing homes, read to them, or help them with daily tasks.
• Protect the environment: Join a beach cleanup, plant trees, or sort recyclables (可回收物).
• Teach others: Tutor (辅导) younger students in subjects you are good at.
• Help animals: Volunteer at an animal shelter or help rescue (救助) stray (流浪) animals.

You don't need to volunteer every day. Even volunteering for just a few hours a week can make a big difference.

As the saying goes, "No one has ever become poor by giving." Start volunteering today, and you will discover that giving is truly receiving.

The Panda: China's National Treasure

The giant panda is one of the most beloved animals in the world. It is also China's national treasure. Pandas live mainly in the mountains of Sichuan, Shaanxi, and Gansu provinces.

Pandas have a distinctive black-and-white coat. This coloration helps them hide in the snowy mountains. Their round bodies and cute faces make them very popular with people. Adult pandas can weigh up to 120 kilograms, but they look much smaller because of their thick fur.

Pandas spend about 14 hours a day eating. Their main food is bamboo. They can eat up to 38 kilograms of bamboo in a single day! However, bamboo has very little nutrition (营养), which is why pandas need to eat so much. Occasionally (偶尔), pandas also eat small animals and fish.

One interesting fact about pandas is that they are good at climbing trees. Even though they look big and slow, they can climb very quickly when they need to.

Pandas are endangered (濒危的) animals. There are only about 1,800 pandas left in the wild. The main threats (威胁) to pandas are habitat loss (栖息地丧失) and low birth rates. Female pandas can only get pregnant for about 2-3 days each year, and baby pandas are very small and weak when they are born.

China has been working hard to protect pandas. The government has set up many nature reserves (自然保护区) where pandas can live safely. Thanks to these efforts, the number of wild pandas has been slowly increasing.

(1) Where do pandas mainly live?
A. In the mountains of Yunnan and Guizhou B. In the mountains of Sichuan, Shaanxi, and Gansu
C. In the forests of northeastern China D. Along the Yangtze River

A. Up to 18 kilograms B. Up to 28 kilograms
C. Up to 38 kilograms D. Up to 48 kilograms

C. Because they need energy to climb trees D. Because their stomachs are very large

(4) How many wild pandas are there approximately?
A. About 1,000 B. About 1,400 C. About 1,600 D. About 1,800

(5) What is China doing to protect pandas?
A. Sending them to other countries B. Setting up nature reserves
C. Feeding them more food D. Building more zoos

(2) C【考点】细节理解【解题思路】第三段给出"up to 38 kilograms"；A18、B28、D48都是看起来合理的数字，需要从原文准确定位
(3) B【考点】细节理解【解题思路】第三段明确解释"bamboo has very little nutrition, which is why pandas need to eat so much"；A错在"only food"，原文说熊猫也吃小动物和鱼；C爬树是额外事实不是吃竹子的原因；D大胃是结果不是原因
(4) D【考点】细节理解【解题思路】第五段说"about 1,800 pandas left in the wild"；A、B、C都是接近但错误的数字，需要精确记忆
(5) B【考点】细节理解【解题思路】最后一段说"set up many nature reserves"；A国际合作不是文中主要措施；C多喂食不是保护策略；D建动物园不是主要保护方式，自然保护才是

To protect the environment, we should:
• Use both sides of paper
• Recycle used paper
• Use digital devices instead of paper when possible
• Buy recycled (回收的) paper products
